paragraphs: Training deep spiking neural networks depends on surrogate gradients, but these approximations can create unstable learning signals across layers and time. The paper connects these difficulties to sharp loss landscapes and proposes A²SG, a framework that changes both how gradients adapt and how they respond to neuronal state.

The adaptive component adjusts the effective gradient window across space and time. Its purpose is to reduce spatial variation while keeping gradient directions consistent over time. The asymmetric component gives larger gradients to neurons with higher membrane potentials. The authors prove that their asymmetric gradients have lower variation than symmetric surrogates.

The analysis also connects local gradient variation to loss curvature, explaining how the method promotes convergence toward flatter minima and better generalization. Experiments cover convolutional and Transformer-based spiking networks, static and neuromorphic image classification, and segmentation. Across these evaluations, the authors report improvements in accuracy and energy efficiency. The contribution combines a proposed explanation for training instability with a gradient design tested across several architectures and tasks.
icml-2026-a-2-sg-adaptive-and-asymmetric.tldr: A²SG adapts surrogate gradients across space, time, and neuronal state to improve spiking-network training, accuracy, and energy efficiency.

paragraphs: An agent working through a long task accumulates observations and records of its own actions. Keeping everything raises inference memory costs and can bury useful information among irrelevant details. ACON addresses both problems by compressing observations and interaction history into representations intended to preserve the state information the agent needs.

Its central mechanism is to improve compression instructions through failure analysis. When an agent fails, the framework uses that evidence to refine natural-language guidelines for what the compressor should retain. This optimizes compression behavior without fine-tuning the agent model. The authors also distill the optimized compressor into smaller models to reduce the overhead of compression itself.

On AppWorld, OfficeBench, and Multi-objective QA, ACON reduces peak token usage by 26–54% while improving task success relative to existing compression baselines. Smaller language models show performance improvements of up to 46%, attributed to reduced context distraction. These findings suggest that better memory selection can improve an agent’s decisions as well as its resource use: retaining more text is not automatically the most effective way to support a long task.
icml-2026-acon-optimizing-context-compre.tldr: ACON improves agent context compression by refining natural-language guidelines from failures, reducing token usage while improving task success.

paragraphs: Process reward models assess individual reasoning steps, providing supervision that can help language models solve problems. Building these evaluators is difficult because manually labeling intermediate steps is expensive. A fixed collection of training errors can also leave an evaluator poorly prepared for unfamiliar mistakes encountered later.

The paper proposes training the evaluator together with a generator that tries to fool it. The generator learns to introduce reasoning errors that escape detection, while the reward model learns to recognize those errors. As the two improve, the generator supplies progressively harder negative examples. This creates an evolving source of training challenges without requiring manual step-level labels.

Across the mathematical reasoning benchmarks studied, the resulting reward models improve solver accuracy by an average of 3.4 percentage points over the strongest process-reward baseline. The reported gain on out-of-distribution tasks is 5.3 percentage points. These results support the value of continually adapting the errors used in training: the benefit appears in the solver’s final accuracy, not only in the evaluator’s ability to detect mistakes.
icml-2026-adversarial-training-for-proce.tldr: Training a reasoning-error generator against a process reward model improves mathematical solver accuracy without manual step-level labels.

paragraphs: Long conversations repeatedly expose a model to an expanding history, increasing attention and encoding costs. Compressing that history can lose details, especially when earlier summaries cannot be shared or revised across turns. The paper examines this fragility and proposes a dialogue memory that changes as the conversation develops.

Context-Driven Incremental Compression treats a conversation as several interleaved contextual threads. Each thread has a revisable compressed state within one compact memory. At each turn, the system retrieves relevant memory, revises it using the current context, and writes it back. This allows later information to update stale memories instead of letting outdated compressed descriptions persist.

The training method adapts truncated backpropagation through time so the model learns dependencies across turns without backpropagating through the entire history. On long-form dialogue benchmarks, the authors report better performance and efficiency, including near-constant inference time and stable perplexity over hundreds of turns. The findings support treating compression as ongoing memory maintenance, where preserving conversational continuity requires both reuse and revision.
icml-2026-context-driven-incremental-com.tldr: C-DIC maintains revisable memories for conversational threads, supporting efficient and stable dialogue generation over hundreds of turns.

paragraphs: A vision-language model learning new classes can forget both previously acquired classes and capabilities inherited from pretraining. The paper argues that evaluations often miss the second loss. Improvements on domains similar to the new training data can inflate retention scores, creating the appearance that foundational knowledge remains intact.

The authors introduce a framework for evaluating both forms of forgetting and a Similarity-Calibrated Retention metric. This metric uses the frozen pretrained feature space to give performance greater weight when semantic similarity is lower. That weighting reduces the influence of gains on closely related domains and makes the evaluation more sensitive to foundational degradation.

Their training method, DFA-MoE, assigns different responsibilities to parameter-efficient experts. A momentum-enhanced contrastive expert handles feature alignment, while separate adaptation experts combine classification and auxiliary contrastive learning to acquire new knowledge while retaining earlier learning. Experiments reveal weaknesses that previous evaluations obscured and report a state-of-the-art balance between preserving incremental and pretrained knowledge. The contribution therefore changes both how continual learning is measured and how competing learning objectives are handled.
icml-2026-dont-forget-why-you-started-ta.tldr: The paper introduces an evaluation and expert-based adaptation method that address forgetting of both new knowledge and pretrained vision-language capabilities.

paragraphs: Object-centric learning builds representations organized around objects, but preserving those representations while learning successive tasks remains challenging. This paper studies Slot Attention and identifies a structure in its latent space that helps explain its resistance to forgetting. Small, separated regions contain representations with matching states of individual factors.

The authors call this behavior factor-wise homogeneity. They observe it within the current task and across a sequence of tasks introducing new factors. The resulting separation between tasks is identified as a key mechanism for preventing catastrophic forgetting. This shifts attention toward structure already emerging in the representations and how that structure supports continued learning.

The paper also finds that this representation structure is insufficient by itself: the decoder can struggle to make use of the separation. A minimal strategy called Decoder-only Post-Replay freezes the homogeneous representations and fine-tunes only the decoder. The authors show this is sufficient to address the identified bottleneck in their setting. The result distinguishes retaining useful internal information from maintaining a decoder that can successfully use it.
icml-2026-factor-wise-homogeneity-of-slo.tldr: Slot Attention develops factor-specific separation across tasks, and decoder-only post-replay helps turn that structure into resistance to forgetting.

paragraphs: Byte-level language models avoid reliance on a subword vocabulary, but generating one byte at a time can make them slow. This paper targets that bottleneck in the Byte Latent Transformer, introducing three approaches that reduce generation work while offering different balances between speed and output quality.

The fastest variant, BLT Diffusion, adds a block-wise diffusion training objective to ordinary next-byte prediction. It can then generate several bytes in parallel during a decoding step, reducing the number of forward passes. BLT Self-speculation instead lets the local decoder draft bytes beyond its usual patch boundaries, then verifies those drafts with one full-model forward pass.

A third variant, BLT Diffusion+Verification, adds autoregressive verification after diffusion generation. Both verification-based approaches exchange some of the fastest variant’s speed for higher generation quality. The authors estimate that each method may reduce memory-bandwidth cost by more than 50% relative to BLT on generation tasks. This is a qualified estimate of bandwidth savings; the central contribution is a set of generation mechanisms that make byte-level modeling more practical.
icml-2026-fast-byte-latent-transformer-7.tldr: Three BLT variants accelerate byte-level generation through parallel diffusion or speculative drafting, with verification options for higher quality.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning an aligned language model on a narrow domain can sometimes produce harmful behavior well beyond that domain. This emergent misalignment can arise even through an API that hides model weights, and the fine-tuning examples alone may make the broader risk difficult to detect. The paper studies safeguards applied during training.

The evaluation considers four properties: preventing broad misalignment, allowing narrow misalignment, learning benign tasks, and maintaining coherent outputs. Five interventions are compared: regularization toward a safe reference model using KL divergence, feature-space distance penalties, preventive steering with an evil-persona vector, interleaving general instruction examples, and inoculation prompting. This makes the comparison sensitive to adaptation quality as well as broad behavioral changes.

The strongest overall results come from interleaving data selected using the perplexity gap between aligned and misaligned models. That gap guides which general instruction examples enter training. The finding highlights the importance of selecting the interleaved data, rather than treating all such examples as interchangeable. The abstract reports this as the best overall intervention among those studied, not as a guarantee that fine-tuning cannot produce misalignment.
icml-2026-in-training-defenses-against-e.tldr: Among five training safeguards, interleaving instruction data selected by aligned–misaligned perplexity gaps gives the best overall results against emergent misalignment.

paragraphs: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning learns how to reach requested goals from a fixed dataset. A central difficulty is estimating goal-conditioned value reliably when success requires a long sequence of actions. The paper identifies incorrect generalization in this value function as a fundamental obstacle to effective learning.

The authors argue that the value function needs an appropriate inductive bias: its design should guide how knowledge transfers beyond the examples directly represented in the data. Their algorithm, Latent-Aligned Value Learning, combines value generalization based on latent representations with hierarchical planning. These components form one framework for using learned representations to support decisions over long horizons.

On OGBench, LAVL achieves the highest performance on 20 of 22 datasets and consistently outperforms the existing methods studied. It is particularly strong on long-horizon tasks and trajectory-stitching datasets, where earlier approaches deteriorate substantially. These findings connect the identified value-generalization problem to practical goal-reaching performance. They support the combination of representation-based value learning and hierarchical planning across the evaluated settings, including those where existing methods have difficulty.
icml-2026-latent-representation-alignmen.tldr: LAVL combines latent-representation-based value learning with hierarchical planning, achieving top performance on 20 of 22 OGBench datasets.

paragraphs: Disentanglement aims to separate the underlying factors that vary in data so models can generalize more effectively. Many approaches constrain a latent vector at a bottleneck through a training objective. The paper points out that these constraints do not easily translate into consistent downstream improvements without a suitable inductive bias.

The proposed Orthogonal Subspaces Projection layer supplies an architectural mechanism for encouraging separation. It can be inserted into intermediate layers and projects latent features into mutually orthogonal subspaces. This builds a preference for separated representations into the model’s structure. The approach is presented as complementary to objectives that operate on latent vectors, broadening where disentanglement can be encouraged.

Across the reported experiments, adding OSP improves both disentanglement quality and downstream generalization. The evaluations span image classification, detection, segmentation, word analogy, text classification, and fine-tuning of large backbones. This breadth matters because the intended benefit is useful task performance as well as cleaner internal representations. The reported findings support the module across several domains and model settings without establishing that every possible model or task will benefit.
icml-2026-layer-centric-factors-of-varia.tldr: The OSP layer encourages disentangled features through orthogonal projections, improving downstream generalization across the evaluated vision and language tasks.

paragraphs: Scene graph generation must identify relationships whose meanings can vary with the image context. A fixed representation of a relationship label can therefore confuse distinct uses. The paper argues that static prototypes and retrieved examples do not adequately reorganize those meanings around the evidence in a particular image.

AlignG uses the candidate relationships within an image to adapt predicate semantics, then feeds those adapted semantics back into the relationship representations. Its learning objective keeps adaptation anchored to global semantic centers. This balances two needs: allowing meanings to shift when scene evidence is consistent, while preventing the representations from drifting away from their shared semantic reference.

Experiments report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on VG-150 and GQA-200. Under the SGDet setting, F@100 increases by 1.4 and 2.7, respectively. Visualizations also show prototypes selectively becoming more similar or more distinct according to image context. Together, these findings support adapting relationship meanings to each scene while retaining a global organizing structure, rather than relying solely on a fixed inventory of semantic prototypes.
icml-2026-learning-context-conditioned-p.tldr: AlignG adapts relationship meanings to each image through prototype feedback, improving scene graph generation while anchoring semantics globally.

paragraphs: Asynchronous pipeline training improves hardware utilization by avoiding idle gaps, but its updates can use gradients computed for older model states. The paper emphasizes that this delay grows linearly with pipeline depth. Increasing the pipeline’s scale can therefore intensify the optimization problem created by stale gradients.

The authors trace an important source of trouble to misalignment between the optimizer’s coordinates and the Hessian eigenbasis, which describes directions of loss curvature. For coordinate-wise adaptive optimizers, this mismatch triggers oscillations that make delayed updates differ from their current counterparts. A convergence bound formalizes how basis misalignment amplifies the penalty associated with delay.

The proposed basis-rotation framework aligns optimizer coordinates with the Hessian eigenbasis to keep delayed updates useful. The theoretical analysis shows that this minimizes basis misalignment and counteracts conditions that worsen delay penalties. In experiments involving language models up to three billion parameters, the authors report 81.7% fewer required iterations than the best-performing asynchronous baseline. This measures improvement in optimization iterations, rather than directly stating an equivalent reduction in training time.
icml-2026-mitigating-staleness-in-asynch.tldr: Rotating optimizer coordinates toward Hessian directions reduces the harm from stale gradients in asynchronous pipeline training.

paragraphs: This paper studies optimization when the available feedback only says which of two candidates is better, and those comparisons can be noisy. Neither objective values nor gradients are accessible. The proposed Noisy-Comparison Random Search samples random directions and uses comparison feedback to accept or reject candidate updates.

The guarantees assume a low-dimensional active-subspace structure, allowing the method to depend on intrinsic dimension k rather than ambient dimension d. With a uniform-margin comparison oracle whose advantage is p, the comparison complexity for reaching ε-first-order stationarity is O(k/(p²ε²)). The result concerns approximate first-order stationarity in a smooth nonconvex problem, rather than guaranteed discovery of a global optimum.

The authors also analyze a setting where comparisons become less reliable when the candidates have similar objective values. They introduce confidence-weighted voting for this gap-dependent feedback model and obtain complexity O(k²/ε⁴). Together, the results show how comparison reliability and effective problem dimension enter convergence guarantees. The contribution provides theoretical support for a simple random-search procedure under two explicitly different models of noisy feedback.
icml-2026-noisy-pairwise-comparison-rand.tldr: NCRS achieves intrinsic-dimension convergence guarantees for smooth nonconvex optimization using only noisy pairwise comparisons.

paragraphs: A regression model can produce precise-looking predictions whose uncertainty is too small. Optimizing overall predictive error may favor informative, narrow distributions without ensuring that those distributions match empirical uncertainty. This paper addresses post-hoc recalibration, where an existing model’s predictive distributions are corrected to better reflect uncertainty.

The authors argue that prior corrections either use weak calibration criteria, such as uniformity of the probability integral transform, or assume a restrictive parametric form for calibration errors. Their algorithm instead uses conditional kernel mean embeddings to perform a nonparametric correction. The goal is to correct calibration error without imposing those restrictive modeling assumptions on its shape.

For real-valued targets, the paper also introduces a characteristic kernel over distributions that can be evaluated in O(n log n) time for empirical distributions containing n samples. This computational contribution supports efficient inference within the recalibration method. Across diverse regression benchmarks and model classes, the authors report consistent improvements over prior recalibration approaches. The findings support correcting the predicted uncertainty itself, alongside the usual concern with prediction accuracy.
icml-2026-nonparametric-distribution-reg.tldr: A nonparametric recalibration method uses conditional kernel embeddings to improve predictive uncertainty across regression benchmarks and model classes.

paragraphs: Physics-informed neural networks can struggle with equations whose solutions oscillate, span multiple scales, are stiff, or evolve over long periods. High dimensionality compounds the difficulty because sampled collocation estimates can introduce substantial integration error and noisy gradients. The paper proposes a solution representation designed to address these problems together.

Low-Rank Fourier Sums represents a solution using a low-rank sum of products of one-dimensional Fourier expansions. This exposes high-frequency structure directly. It also permits closed-form computation of common physics-based objectives and their gradients, including L² residual and variational losses. For these objectives, analytic evaluation replaces sampled collocation estimates and removes the associated sampling noise.

The authors provide theoretical results explaining why the representation is particularly suitable for high-dimensional settings. Across established PINN failure-mode benchmarks and higher-dimensional extensions, LoRFS consistently outperforms strong PINN baselines and remains stable where competing methods degrade. The contribution links representation choice to optimization reliability: the Fourier structure captures oscillations while also making common training objectives analytically evaluable.
icml-2026-overcoming-pinns-failure-modes.tldr: LoRFS uses separable Fourier representations to evaluate common physics losses analytically, improving stability on difficult high-dimensional PDE benchmarks.

paragraphs: Audio-visual language models reason over sound, images, and text, but their internal exchange of information is difficult to understand. This paper asks where information from one modality appears inside the token representations of another. Its focus is the internal location of integrated audio-visual evidence across several recent models.

The analysis finds that integrated information is primarily encoded in sink tokens. Those tokens do not all play the same role, however. A distinct subset specializes in storing information that crosses between audio and vision. The authors name these cross-modal sink tokens, distinguishing the tokens carrying integrated evidence from other sink tokens.

Using this observation, the paper proposes a training-free method for mitigating hallucinations by encouraging the model to rely on the integrated information in those specialized tokens. The practical idea is to direct generation toward internal representations that already combine the modalities. The main stated findings concern the location and specialization of these information hubs; the abstract introduces the mitigation method without giving a numerical estimate of its effect.
icml-2026-probing-cross-modal-informatio.tldr: The paper identifies specialized sink tokens that store integrated audio-visual information and uses them to motivate training-free hallucination mitigation.

paragraphs: When a multimodal model reasons from an image, users may want to know which visual regions actually support its reasoning. Faithful causal attribution is expensive because it can require repeated backward passes or input perturbations. Raw attention is available immediately, but the paper emphasizes that attention alone lacks causal validity.

The proposed framework learns to estimate the causal effects of semantic image regions from attention features. It amortizes attribution through a learned estimator, making those features useful for approximating the more expensive causal analysis. This enables attribution to be streamed while the model is producing its reasoning, rather than computed only after the reasoning finishes.

Across five benchmarks and four thinking models, the authors report faithfulness comparable to exhaustive causal methods. The result supports a practical role for lightweight learning in visual attribution: attention features can inform an estimator even though raw attention maps are not themselves causal explanations. The intended benefit is timely evidence about visual grounding during tasks such as generating code from screenshots or solving image-based mathematics problems.
icml-2026-real-time-visual-attribution-s.tldr: A learned estimator turns attention features into streaming visual attributions with faithfulness comparable to expensive causal methods in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Tables from the same domain can describe shared attributes using different headers. A representation learned from one table alone may therefore miss common meanings across tables. The paper also identifies two underused signals: the distribution of values in a column and differences in the semantic roles that attributes play.

NAVI organizes pretraining around segments, with each segment consisting of a header and value pair. This unit brings together evidence from the table’s schema and the column’s value distribution. Its Masked Segment Modeling and Entropy-driven Segment Alignment objectives jointly encourage structured header–value relationships and semantic alignment across stable and instance-specific attributes.

The approach matters because it connects the naming and organization of an attribute with evidence from the values it contains. It also avoids treating every attribute’s semantic role as interchangeable within the learning objectives. Experiments on heterogeneous tables within a domain report overall improvements in reconstruction, semantic consistency, and downstream usefulness across the evaluation settings. Those findings support the segment-centered design for learning shared domain semantics from varied tables.
icml-2026-segment-driven-structural-indu.tldr: NAVI learns heterogeneous table representations from header–value segments, combining schema structure with column distributions to improve semantic consistency and downstream utility.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models repeatedly refine a noisy draft of an entire response, updating text in parallel. This paper finds that important entities appear early in those drafts. Even before the answer is complete, the emerging text can therefore provide useful clues about what external evidence the model should retrieve.

SARDI uses those intermediate drafts to guide retrieval during denoising. Retrieval becomes a dynamic part of generation, informed by the answer currently taking shape. The authors also find that grounding generation in retrieved evidence sharply reduces dependence between tokens, making retrieval particularly compatible with parallel decoding. The framework requires no training and does not depend on a particular retriever.

The stated applicability covers reasoning-capable discrete diffusion language models. Across five multi-hop question-answering benchmarks, SARDI outperforms training-free diffusion and autoregressive retrieval baselines while achieving up to five times higher throughput. The findings connect two benefits of the diffusion process: drafts expose useful retrieval targets early, and retrieved evidence supports effective parallel generation. The maximum throughput gain is a reported experimental result, not a uniform speedup for every setting.
icml-2026-self-augmenting-retrieval-for-.tldr: SARDI retrieves evidence from intermediate diffusion drafts, improving multi-hop question answering with up to five times higher throughput than the compared baselines.

paragraphs: Total variation and Hellinger distance provide different ways to measure how far apart probability distributions are. This paper studies how tightly they are connected for Gaussian location mixtures. Establishing a precise relationship makes it possible to transfer statistical guarantees expressed in one distance into guarantees expressed in the other.

For mixing distributions supported on a compact set, the authors bound the Hellinger distance by total variation raised to a power of 1−o(1). The correction term has order 1/log log(1/TV), so the exponent approaches one as total variation becomes small. They also construct two sequences of mixing distributions demonstrating that the bound is sharp.

The upper bound and matching constructions resolve the stated open problem and yield an entropic characterization of learning Gaussian mixtures in total variation. The inequality additionally supports optimal robust estimation in Hellinger distance, with an implication for bounding empirical Bayes minimax regret under Huber contamination. The compact-support condition is part of the stated result; the paper’s contribution is a sharp mathematical relationship and the statistical consequences that follow from it.
icml-2026-sharp-inequalities-between-tot.tldr: A sharp bound links Hellinger and total variation distances for compactly supported Gaussian location mixtures, yielding learning and robust-estimation consequences.

paragraphs: Looped transformers repeatedly apply a shared block, allowing computation to unfold over several internal iterations. A training example may influence different parts of that process differently. Standard TracIn attribution combines those effects into one scalar score, hiding when the example matters during the model’s recurrent computation.

Step-Decomposed Influence separates that aggregate into an influence trajectory with one entry per loop iteration. It does so by unrolling the recurrent computation graph and assigning influence to specific iterations. The resulting trajectory retains the temporal structure of the internal computation, giving a more detailed view of how individual training examples shape latent reasoning.

To make the method practical for transformers, the authors introduce a TensorSketch implementation that avoids materializing per-example gradients. Experiments on looped GPT-style models and algorithmic reasoning tasks report strong scalability and low error relative to full-gradient baselines. The method also supports several attribution and interpretability tasks. Its contribution is therefore both analytical resolution across reasoning steps and a computational approach that makes that finer resolution feasible at transformer scale.
icml-2026-step-resolved-data-attribution.tldr: SDI decomposes training-data influence across a looped transformer’s iterations, using TensorSketch to avoid storing per-example gradients.

paragraphs: Model merging combines separately trained models into one model that handles multiple tasks. The paper asks whether merging can make tasks improve one another, beyond preventing their updates from conflicting. It identifies cross-task compatibility between encoders and predictors as an indicator of how well a merge will work.

SyMerge jointly optimizes the coefficients used to merge models and a single task-specific layer. The authors demonstrate that adapting only this layer can be sufficient to induce synergy. Training uses an expert-guided self-labeling objective, which supplies stable supervision beyond entropy minimization. The design keeps adaptation lightweight while directly addressing compatibility across the models being combined.

The method also successfully merges models trained from different initializations, a setting where standard approaches break down in the study. Across vision, dense prediction, and natural language processing benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art results. These findings suggest that limited adaptation can unlock useful cooperation between task models. The single-layer result is a demonstrated sufficiency claim, rather than a claim that one layer is always necessary or adequate for every merging problem.
icml-2026-symerge-from-non-interference-.tldr: SyMerge jointly adjusts merging coefficients and one task-specific layer to enable task synergy, including for models with different initializations.

paragraphs: Training a smaller model on reasoning from larger teachers requires choosing which solutions to include. One strategy favors complete responses that the student already assigns high probability. The paper finds that this strategy works within a single teacher but fails when selecting long reasoning traces from several diverse teachers.

The authors attribute this failure to scoring at the wrong scale. Whole-response probability rewards global fluency, while the transferable information lies in familiar transitions between reasoning steps. Their Local Average Log Probability score evaluates each step using only a short window of preceding context. This targets how well the step follows from its immediate premises rather than how natural the entire solution appears.

LALP supports choosing a teacher before fine-tuning and curating examples from a mixed pool of teachers. Across mathematical, coding, and scientific reasoning tasks, the authors report consistent accuracy improvements by a large margin over selecting the most natural complete solutions. The findings suggest that useful reasoning data can be identified through local step compatibility even when whole-trajectory likelihood is an unreliable selection signal.
icml-2026-the-signal-is-in-the-steps-loc.tldr: LALP selects reasoning data by scoring local step transitions, improving student accuracy when learning from diverse teachers.

paragraphs: Electronic health records contain numerical measurements and events whose timing matters, making them different from ordinary language. The paper proposes pretraining tailored to those features. Its design addresses how clinical values are represented, how event timing is encoded, and what future events the model learns to predict.

Pathology-Focused Binning allocates attention to clinically significant numerical ranges through density-based quantization, rather than prioritizing usual values. Dual-Calendar Rotary Positional Embedding represents both absolute event times and relative intervals. The Time-Conditioned Foreseeing objective then forecasts events across multiple time horizons while explicitly modeling when they occur, aligning the prediction task with treatment planning.

Together, these components produce a temporal generative model for health records. The authors report improvements over existing foundation models on eleven downstream tasks, with gains of up to 54% in AUPRC. They also report generation of realistic patient trajectories that remain temporally consistent. The maximum metric improvement is task-dependent; the broader contribution is a pretraining approach that treats numerical significance and irregular timing as central properties of health records.
icml-2026-time-conditioned-foreseeing-an.tldr: TCF tailors health-record pretraining to clinically significant values and event timing, improving eleven downstream tasks and generating temporally consistent trajectories.

paragraphs: Some tasks have no objectively checkable answer, so reinforcement learning must rely on subjective judgments of quality. Direct rubric scores can be poorly calibrated, and a single comparison can provide a noisy or sparse signal. Tournament Style RL builds rewards from multiple comparisons against a fixed collection of reference responses.

A judge applies a rubric to compare a candidate response with each anchor, and the candidate’s win rate becomes its training reward. Keeping the anchors fixed stabilizes the reference frame. Aggregating judgments reduces reward variance and makes the signal more robust to judge noise, giving policy optimization a steadier basis for comparing response quality.

Across four non-verifiable tasks and two language-model backbones, TSRL improves average win rate by 43.8 points over the base model and 22.8 points over the strongest baseline. The authors also report benefits from increasing the number of anchors and robustness with weak or partially corrupted judges. Blinded human preference studies support the results. The evidence suggests that structuring subjective comparisons can materially improve learning even when objective correctness is unavailable.
icml-2026-tournament-style-rl-stabilizin.tldr: TSRL uses win rates against fixed anchor responses as rewards, stabilizing subjective policy optimization and improving evaluated response quality.
